subject: Observability plan for on-prem VPC deployment / SIEM & tracing
messages:
From: Anika Rao <anika@acme-finserv.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Jared Cole <jared.cole@acme-finserv.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T16:12:00Z
Subject: Observability for Redwood Private deployment (on-prem VPC)

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the quick onboarding so far. We start air-gapped provisioning next week and need to lock down how logs/metrics/traces will be exported into our Splunk HEC (behind a reverse proxy) and our internal tracing stack. A couple constraints up front:

- No general internet egress from the host subnet; only allowed TLS to a small set of IPs via a proxy.
- Splunk HEC endpoint is internal (10.10.45.12) reachable only through a forwarder tier.
- Data residency: logs containing user prompts are subject to redaction and 90-day retention.
- We need an approach that avoids shipping raw prompt text to any third-party SaaS.

Can you outline concrete options (agent/sidecar vs centralized forwarder, network patterns, what needs NAT/VPC endpoints, and how tracing/OTLP should be set up) and call out any blockers for our security team (cc'd). Also include a short verification plan we can run in staging.

Thanks,
Anika Rao
Senior Platform Engineer
Acme FinServ

--
Attachment: initial-constraints.xlsx (spreadsheet listing approved egress IPs)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Anika Rao <anika@acme-finserv.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-19T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Observability for Redwood Private deployment (on-prem VPC)

Hi Anika,

Appreciate the constraints summary — below is a concise options matrix plus a recommended plan tailored to the no-egress / internal-HEC requirement. I attached a diagram (redwood-private-forwarder-design-v1.pdf) and a sample OTLP config for your tracing team.

Summary of options (tradeoffs):

1) Sidecar agent per node (agent-based)
   - Pattern: run OTel collector and log agent (Filebeat/Fluent Bit) as a sidecar on each compute host or in the same k8s pod as the model runtime.
   - Network: sidecars call internal Splunk forwarder / HEC over TLS. No internet egress required.
   - Pros: lowest latency, easier local redaction/filtering (drop prompts at the edge), resilient to intermittent aggregator failures.
   - Cons: more operational footprint, needs config distribution and certificate management per node.

2) Centralized forwarder (aggregator) inside customer VPC
   - Pattern: model hosts push to a small set of hardened forwarders (stateful aggregator tier) that handle batching, redaction, and proxy egress. Forwarders then send to Splunk HEC/internal tracing backends.
   - Network: restrict compute hosts to talk only to aggregator IPs; aggregators need egress to HEC IPs or internal load balancer.
   - Pros: simpler host configs, single place to rotate tokens and run HSM-backed encryption, easier to throttle and audit.
   - Cons: single point to size/scale, need HA and careful failover.

3) Agentless pull + secure staging store (fallback)
   - Pattern: hosts write to encrypted S3/object store inside VPC; forwarder pulls and ships. Useful if direct TCP to HEC is blocked but S3 is allowed.
   - Pros: avoids persistent forwarding connections, good for offline air-gapped flows.
   - Cons: added delayed delivery, more storage/retention management.

My recommendation: Centralized forwarder tier inside your VPC as the primary pattern, with sidecar agents as optional canary/critical-host pattern. Centralized forwarders give you one place to implement strict redaction, token lifecycle, and HSM/KMS integration.

Network & security specifics:
- Egress: Forwarders must be in a network zone that can reach Splunk HEC (10.10.45.12) via the approved proxy. Use NAT or dedicated egress SGs as required by your firewall policy.
- TLS/mTLS: Use mTLS between hosts and forwarders. Forwarders present customer-managed certs (rotate via your ACME or internal CA). Use HEC tokens between forwarders and Splunk and rotate tokens monthly.
- AuthN/AuthZ: Integrate forwarder with your KMS/HSM for encrypting long-term archives and secrets. Redwood can sign a small verification package for our components if you want to pin binaries.
- Redaction: Implement prompt-redaction at the forwarder using the sample regex rules in the attached acme-obsv-mapping.xlsx. Keep a minimal, hashed audit trail if required.
- Metrics: Export runtime metrics as Prometheus exposition format to the forwarder; forwarder scrapes or pulls metrics and transforms to your monitoring backend. Alternatively, push metrics over pushgateway to the internal collector.
- Tracing: Run an OTLP collector on the forwarder. Sampling should be local (head-sampled) with sampler rules we can tune. For production, sample at 0.1-1% by default and increase for error traces.

Operational/verification plan (staging):
1) Deploy a single HA forwarder pair in staging with mTLS certs and HEC connectivity.
2) Configure a test service to emit logs, metrics, and traces. Validate redaction rules remove prompt text.
3) Run a fault injection: kill one forwarder and confirm failover and no log loss above SLA threshold.
4) Validate retention: run a data sweep test to ensure prompt-containing logs older than 90 days are purged.
5) Run a partial canary with sidecar agents on 5% of hosts to compare latency and determine whether to adopt sidecars broadly.

Owners & next steps:
- Redwood: Karthik Iyer (design + canary support), Marissa Cole (runtime config + docs)
- Acme: Anika Rao (networking), Jared Cole (security review)

I attached: redwood-private-forwarder-design-v1.pdf, sample-otlp-config.yaml, and a suggested mapping spreadsheet. If this looks good I can put together Terraform snippets for the forwarder ASG, security groups, and IAM roles.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer

Date: 2027-04-20T15:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Observability for Redwood Private deployment (on-prem VPC)

Hi team,

Quick security notes from Acme's perspective that we should confirm before design lock:

- PII & Prompt Redaction: Are we able to guarantee in-band redaction of prompt text prior to any aggregation or transient persistence? If not, we need to add an encrypted transient buffer with strict access controls and automatic scrub on ingest.
- Audit logs: We require an immutable audit trail for redaction decisions and forwarder auth events. Can forwarders push signed audit events to a separate write-once store?
- Key management: Customer-managed keys are required for any archives exported out of the VPC. Redwood must support HSM-backed key wrapping for secrets at rest.
- SOC2 evidence: We will ask for configuration samples that show TLS/mTLS enforcement, token rotation logs, and the retention purge job schedule during our SOC2 checklist review.

If Redwood can provide the Terraform snippets + an example purge job and an explanation of how redaction is provably irreversible (we prefer irreversible hash + salt pattern for audit artifacts), we can proceed to architecture approval.

Laura Bennett
Security Engineering Manager
Redwood Inference
